findings.element: RevRec · Schedule details table, Schedule start column of row sub_after_release_3c1b
findings.finding: After the user confirms a new Schedule start date, the existing schedule row is re-dated, which contradicts the modal they just confirmed ('Existing recognition schedules keep their current dates').
findings.user_impact: The user cannot trust either the modal or the table to tell them what the change actually does to existing schedules, and this is exactly the question the primary task asks them to answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave existing rows' Schedule start unchanged on confirm, so the table matches the going-forward-only rule the modal states.

evidence.action: On RevRec, pick Schedule start = Invoice issued date, then Confirm; repeat with Payment date + Confirm
evidence.observed: Row sub_after_release_3c1b's Schedule start changes from '28 Dec 2025' to '6 Jan 2026', then to 'Payment date', after the modal said existing schedules keep their dates

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab · RevRec lock: 'Change Schedule start date instead →' escape route
findings.finding: Following the lock's own instructions does not unlock Invoice date: after Schedule start is confirmed as Payment date, the PT select is still disabled and the lock message still shows.
findings.user_impact: A user who does exactly what the lock message says loops between two screens and still cannot change Invoice date.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the PT lock from the current Schedule start value, so confirming Payment date re-enables the Invoice date select and removes the lock message.

evidence.action: In PT · RevRec lock, click 'Change Schedule start date instead →', set Schedule start = Payment date and Confirm, then return to PT · RevRec lock
evidence.observed: Invoice date select is still disabled=true and the lock message is still visible=true; the lock is a fixed variant, not derived from Schedule start

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab (and Sales tab): Invoice date select vs. Update button
findings.finding: The Invoice date select saves as soon as it changes, but the same tab also has an Update button that shows its own 'Settings updated' toast, so the tab has two save models.
findings.user_impact: Users can't tell whether a change is already committed or still waits for Update, so some will click Update unnecessarily and others will distrust the auto-save.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one save model per tab: either Invoice date commits through Update like the rest of the tab, or the Update button does not appear alongside auto-saving selects.

evidence.action: Change Invoice date to Created date, then click Update
evidence.observed: First a 'Saved' toast appears on change, then a second toast 'Settings updated' appears on Update

findings.element: PT · Invoices tab · Pro: Invoice date row (help sentence, defaults caption, info callout)
findings.finding: One select carries three stacked text blocks, and the defaults caption ('Existing connections stay on Created date') contradicts the value shown (Issued date) without saying whether this is a new or an existing connection.
findings.user_impact: The user has to read about 70 words to work one select, and still can't tell whether Issued date is their current setting or a default that hasn't applied yet.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut the row to the label and the select, and let the selected value alone show the connection's actual current state.

evidence.action: Open variant pt-pro and read the Invoice date row
evidence.observed: The row shows a New badge, a help sentence, a grey caption saying existing connections stay on Created date, and a blue info callout, while the select's initial value is Issued date

findings.finding: 'Schedule start date' is shown twice (section heading and row label), each with its own description, plus a 'Sync lock:' paragraph, an 'Issued date column' note and the 'invented chrome (not live in demo)' header line, so the screen has several competing explanation blocks around one select.
findings.user_impact: The single control the user came to change gets lost among duplicated headings and explanatory paragraphs, which slows scanning and blurs what the primary action is.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a single 'Schedule start date' label with its select and remove the duplicated heading description, the Sync lock and Issued date column paragraphs, and the prototype annotation line.
